name: Starship HLS propellant depot
note: Parity model for the v1.1 'Starship HLS Depot' type. Body frame: +Z = long axis toward the nose, origin at the aft dome. A 9 m stainless body of revolution with a body-mounted solar band; no flaps, no heat shield. The stretch, the band and the attitude are estimates; the skin is bare steel until the depot's insulating tiles are described.

sources.subject: attitude
sources.value: nose along velocity (least drag at 281 km), +X toward nadir (roll is irrelevant to a body of revolution)
sources.source: No published depot attitude. The v1.1 legacy type was nadir-pointing. HLS points its nose at the Sun for its deployable arrays (Wikipedia, 'Starship HLS'), but a body-mounted band gains nothing from that. Estimate.

sources.subject: body
sources.value: one rigid group: no flaps, no heat shield, no deployables
sources.source: Wikipedia, 'Starship HLS': HLS and the depot 'do not re-enter Earth's atmosphere, which allows for the removal of the spacecraft's atmospheric heat shield and flight control surfaces (fins)'.

sources.value: 9 m diameter barrel, 48 m (a stretched Starship tank section)
sources.source: Starship's 9 m diameter (SpaceX). Length: the depot is 'a taller tanker' (Wikipedia, 'Orbital propellant depot' / Starship HLS) - the stretch is unpublished; 60 m overall here vs ~50 m for a Starship ship (estimate, range 50-70 m).

sources.subject: nose_cone
sources.value: 12 m cone from 4.5 m to a 0.6 m tip (the ogive as a cone)
sources.source: Starship's nose is an ogive ~12 m tall; the cone is the primitive nearest it (a cone over-states the flat facets' area slightly).

sources.subject: solar_band
sources.value: 4 m band of body-mounted cells around the barrel near the top
sources.source: Wikipedia, 'Starship HLS': 'Electrical power is supplied by a band of solar panels around the circumference of the vehicle' (HLS). That the depot shares it, the band height and its position are ESTIMATES.

sources.subject: depot_skin
sources.value: bare stainless (the new stainless_steel preset, ring-weld seams)
sources.source: The depot uses 'a special purpose insulating tile' for MMOD and cryogenic insulation (Wikipedia, 'Starship HLS'); its coverage and colour are unpublished, so the flight-proven bare 304L exterior stands in. Swap this one material when depot imagery exists.
